fact: The NIA, with the Births and Deaths Registry and Ghana Health Service, tested on 11 August 2026 a renewed application to register children aged 0-5 at selected health facilities and issue them Ghana PINs, a programme launched in March 2024 and suspended after a technical fault, with full rollout expected in the coming days.

The Vice President launched the Ghana Card Number at Birth system, giving newborns a unique identification number at birth, with biometric details captured at health facilities where e-tracking is deployed (338 facilities).
Bedzrah said NIA was extending the system to children from birth and would begin registering children aged 0-5 the following week, after the ongoing registration of ages 6-14.

NIA Executive Secretary Wisdom Kwaku Deku said the NIA is preparing to begin registration at hospitals where parents or guardians would receive an identity number for newborns, later linked to the child's Ghana Card registration at age six.
